snip.t: Anaphylaxis Protocol: Administer intramuscular adrenaline immediately into the anterolateral thigh; avoid intravenous boluses unless trained and cardiac monitoring is attached.

•There is no direct sympathetic innervation of the smooth muscle of the bronchi, and antagonism of parasympathetically induced bronchoconstriction is critically dependent upon circulating epinephrine (adrenaline) acting through β2- receptors on the surface of smooth muscle cells.
For severe or life-threatening asthma: IV magnesium sulphate, IV salbutamol or aminophylline, adrenaline, and admission to the high-dependency unit, with ventilation if exhausted.

qs.q: Which specific G-protein subtype is initially activated upon adrenaline binding to its G-protein-coupled receptor?
qs.e: Adrenaline binding to its GPCR activates the Gs subtype of G-proteins. The Gi subtype is typically inhibitory and is not involved in this specific step.

qs.q: A 42-year-old man presents with episodic headaches, excessive sweating, and palpitations associated with severe hypertension. Further evaluation confirms a catecholamine-secreting tumour located in the adrenal medulla. Which key enzyme is responsible for converting noradrenaline to adrenaline specifically within this tissue?
qs.e: Phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase is the key enzyme that converts noradrenaline to adrenaline and is found exclusively in the adrenal medulla. Tyrosine hydroxylase catalyses the rate-limiting step earlier in catecholamine biosynthesis.
